text:
Maria Chen: Kicked off a small canary comparing model v2.1-int4 (quantized) against v2.0-fp16 for the docs/summarization flows. initial sample = 2k requests, 5% traffic. quick snapshot: latency p95 +18ms, avg latency +12ms, MRR delta -1.3% overall, hallucination alerts +0.6% on the long-doc slice.
Sam Patel: thanks — any signal above our auto-fallback? :thinking_face:
Maria Chen: current auto-fallback config is conservative: mrr_drop_pct: 2.0, hallucination_pct_delta: 1.0, latency_p95_ms_increase: 20. deploy-bot started canary at 1758643201 :rocket:
deploy-bot: Canary started: v2.1-int4 vs v2.0-fp16, 5% traffic, monitoring hooks enabled. Logs -> https://internal.redwood/canaries/1758643201
Lee Johnson: raw numbers please (slice breakdown)?
Maria Chen: paste but trimmed:
```
slice: long-docs
  baseline MRR: 0.364
  candidate MRR: 0.359
  delta: -1.4%
  hallucination alerts: baseline 0.8% -> candidate 1.6% (+0.8pp)
  p95 latency baseline: 210ms -> candidate 230ms (+20ms)
slice: short-answers
  delta MRR: -0.6%
  hallucination: baseline 0.3% -> candidate 0.4%
```
Sam Patel: hmm long-doc hallucination +0.8pp exceeds the hallucination_pct_delta=1.0? it's below but close. p95 is right on the limit if config is +20ms.
Lee Johnson: our rule is two-strike: either mrr_drop_pct OR hallucination_pct_delta tripped will trigger instant fallback. since mrr drop is -1.4% and threshold is -2.0%, we wouldn't auto-fallback yet. but hallucination jumped 0.8pp (threshold 1.0pp) — borderline.
Maria Chen: proposal: tighten hallucination threshold for long-doc slice only to 0.5pp during early canary. also add a multi-metric rule: require MRR drop >1.5% AND hallucination >0.5pp for immediate fallback. otherwise alert and hold.
Sam Patel: I like that. reduces noisy rollbacks but protects long-doc quality. can we add a hysteresis window so a single spike doesn't flip? e.g., require the trigger for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.
Maria Chen: yes. example config I pushed to the gatebook:
```
canary_gate:
  selectors:
    - slice: long-docs
  rules:
    - name: early-guard-long-docs
      metrics:
        - metric: mrr_delta_pct
          threshold: -1.5
          comparator: "<="
        - metric: hallucination_pp_delta
          threshold: 0.5
          comparator: ">="
      window_minutes: 5
      consecutive_windows: 3
      action: "auto_fallback"
```
deploy-bot: Gate config updated: refs/gates/1758643201/early-guard-long-docs
Lee Johnson: sounds reasonable. one nit: use absolute hallucination_pp instead of delta? delta can be noisy on tiny baselines. for slices with baseline <1% we should use absolute >1.0% check.
Maria Chen: good call. I'll make rule hybrid: if baseline_hallucination_pct < 1.0 then use absolute threshold 1.0pp, else use delta 0.5pp. will document.
Sam Patel: any A/B quality sig tests (statistical)?
Maria Chen: ran a quick bootstrap on MRR; p-value ~0.12 for overall 2k sample (underpowered for slice-level long-doc). ordering: need ~8k samples to detect 1% MRR with 80% power. I'm increasing canary sample to 15% for next 30m to accelerate.
Lee Johnson: careful with traffic ramp but ok for 30m. ops aware?
Maria Chen: pinging ops now. @Sam @Lee I'll post updated gate config and a short runbook change for the long-doc special-case.
Sam Patel: fine. also add a metric for human flagged hallucinations from feedback pipeline — that tends to catch semantic errors missed by our rule.
Maria Chen: added. final action: 1) tighten long-doc early-guard as above, 2) require 3 consecutive 5-min windows, 3) hybrid absolute/delta hallucination comparator, 4) bump sample to 15% for 30m. rollback if auto_fallback triggers or MRR p-value < 0.05 after 30m.
Lee Johnson: ack. schedule a follow-up check at 1758643620.
Maria Chen: noted — will post results. :thumbsup:
